claim.pdf_says: Under General rule 15) the continuation sentence 'When the file sharing conflict condition exists as a result of the DELETE FILE statement:' and the sub-items 'a) The file is not deleted, and may be accessed.', 'b) The valu62’ is placed into the I-O status ...', 'c) The DELETE FILE statement is unsuccessful.' are all indented one level in from the '15)' rule number, i.e. printed as children of rule 15).
claim.markdown_says:
15) If file locking is in effect for file-name-1 ...

When the file sharing conflict condition exists as a result of the DELETE FILE statement:

a) The file is not deleted, and may be accessed.

b) The valu62' is placed into the I-O status associated with file-name-1 to indicate the file operation conflict condition.

c) The DELETE FILE statement is unsuccessful.

(all flush left, zero indentation — ISO_COBOL.md lines 26418-26426)
claim.why_it_matters: The four child blocks are detached from their parent rule and sit at the same indentation as the top-level numbered rules, so a) b) c) read as free-standing items rather than as the consequences of the file sharing conflict condition described in rule 15). The transcription indents this exact structure correctly elsewhere in the same statement — the a)/b)/c) under GR 6 on page 636 and under GR 20/21 on page 638 all carry the three-space indent — so page 637 is the outlier, not the convention.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED — the difference is leading whitespace only; no content is missing, added, reordered, or attached to a different rule. (1) PDF geometry measured, not eyeballed: on spec_p637.png (300 dpi, 2550x3300) the top-level rule-number column is x=336-338 ('8)', '9)', '10)', '11)', 'FORMAT 2', '12)', '13)', '14)', '15)'), the first indent level is x=407-411, and the second is x=481-482. The four disputed blocks measure left=407 ('When the file sharing conflict condition exists as a result of the DELETE FILE statement:'), left=408 ('a)'), left=408 ('b)', continuation 'conflict condition.' at 481) and left=409 ('c)'). So the claim's description of the PDF is factually correct: those blocks are printed one level (about 70 px / 0.23 in) in from the '15)' number. (2) The markdown is also quoted correctly — lines 26423-26429 are flush left (the claim cites 26418-26426, off by five, a location misquote but the quoted text is verbatim). (3) But the claim is scoped wrong and mislabelled. Nothing is MISPLACED: every word and every list label a)/b)/c) is present, in the printed order, immediately following rule 15) and immediately preceding rule 16), which resumes on page 638. Text-for-text the two sources agree exactly — including the ISO PDF's own glyph corruption, which the render confirms is printed in the PDF as 'The valu62’ is placed' (an ISO defect, faithfully transcribed; the same phenomenon prints as 'is set t37’' in GR 16 on page 638). (4) The indent loss is a whole-page transcription artifact, not a rule-15 defect: EVERY indented line on page 637 lost its indent, not just the block under GR 15. Line 26401 ('2. A lock held by that file connector on another record ...', printed at x=482, i.e. two levels in) and line 26403 ('b) If multiple record locking ...', printed at x=408) are equally flush left in the markdown — both are the page-break continuation of GR 7's a)/1./2. hierarchy from page 636. So the finding as filed describes one symptom of a page-wide formatting drop while asserting it is specific to GR 15. (5) The indent is cosmetic even where the transcription 'gets it right'. The file uses plain paragraphs here, not markdown lists; CommonMark strips 1-3 leading spaces from a paragraph, so the page-636 block ('   a) The record is not logically removed, and may be accessed.') renders byte-identically to the page-637 block. The three-space indent encodes no structure that any consumer of ISO_COBOL.md can read. (6) Subordination survives unambiguously in the transcription: the lead-in sentence terminates in a colon and is immediately followed by a), b), c); and top-level General Rules in 14.9.10.4 are NUMBERED throughout ('14)', '15)', '16)', ... '21)') and never lettered, so a lettered item cannot be misread as a top-level rule. No COBOL semantics derivable from GR 15 change. Per the reject criteria this is formatting, not a content discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. PDF and markdown agree word-for-word on GR 15 and its a)/b)/c) consequences (including the ISO PDF's own printed corruption 'The valu62’'). The only difference is that the markdown transcription of page 637 dropped ALL leading indentation for the entire page — not merely the GR 15 children, but also line 26401 ('2. A lock held ...', printed two levels in) and line 26403 ('b) If multiple record locking ...', printed one level in), which are the page-break continuation of GR 7. If this is ever re-filed it should be filed as a cosmetic whole-page indentation-normalization item for page 637, severity trivial, not as structural misplaced content: the indent is stripped by CommonMark anyway, the lettered items follow a colon-terminated lead-in, and the top-level rules in this section are numbered rather than lettered, so no hierarchy is actually ambiguous.
